explanation: Bisulphite (hydrogen sulphite) is HSO₃⁻ (valency 1) and calcium is Ca²⁺, so the formula is Ca(HSO₃)₂. Ca(HSO₄)₂ is calcium bisulphate.

text: Fertilisers with more nitrogen content are considered better. Comparing urea (NH₂CONH₂) and ammonium phosphate [(NH₄)₃PO₄], which is better and what is its percentage of nitrogen? [N = 14, H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, P = 31]
explanation: Urea: M = 60, N = 28, so %N = 28/60 × 100 = 46.67%. Ammonium phosphate: M = 3(18) + 31 + 64 = 149, N = 42, so %N = 42/149 × 100 = 28.19%. Urea has more nitrogen.

text: The percentage composition of sodium plumbite (Na₂PbO₂) is: [Na = 23, Pb = 207, O = 16]

Conc. sulphuric acid is added to (X) blue vitriol, which turns into a white anhydrous salt, and (Y) hydrogen chloride gas containing water droplets, which loses its moisture without forming any new product. The role of conc. sulphuric acid in X and in Y is respectively:
explanation: In X the acid removes the water of crystallisation chemically from CuSO₄·5H₂O, acting as a dehydrating agent. In Y it only absorbs the moisture present with the gas, so the HCl gas becomes dry: it acts as a drying agent.

text: How can zinc sulphate and ferrous sulphate solutions be distinguished using sodium hydroxide solution?
options: ZnSO₄ gives a white gelatinous ppt soluble in excess NaOH; FeSO₄ gives a dirty green ppt insoluble in excess
ZnSO₄ gives a dirty green ppt; FeSO₄ gives a white ppt soluble in excess
ZnSO₄ gives a reddish-brown ppt; FeSO₄ gives a blue ppt
Both give white ppts soluble in excess
explanation: Zn²⁺ gives white Zn(OH)₂, which dissolves in excess NaOH forming sodium zincate. Fe²⁺ gives dirty green Fe(OH)₂, which does not dissolve in excess.

text: The formula and charge of the nitride ion and the nitrite ion are respectively:
explanation: Nitride is N³⁻ (charge −3). Nitrite is NO₂⁻ (charge −1). NO₃⁻ is nitrate.

text: A certain mass of a gas occupies 2 litres at 27 °C and 100 atm. At what temperature will its volume and pressure both become half of their initial values?
explanation: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂ ⇒ T₂ = T₁ × (P₂/P₁) × (V₂/V₁) = 300 × ½ × ½ = 75 K = 75 − 273 = −198 °C.

text: The balanced equation for the reaction of aluminium with copper sulphate solution is:
explanation: Aluminium is trivalent, so aluminium sulphate is Al₂(SO₄)₃. Al is more reactive than Cu and displaces it: 2Al + 3CuSO₄ → Al₂(SO₄)₃ + 3Cu.

text: The products formed on the photolytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide are:
explanation: In light, 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂. This is why hydrogen peroxide is stored in dark bottles.

text: The formula of gypsum is:
explanation: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O. CaSO₄·½H₂O is plaster of Paris.

text: The chemical formula of Epsom salt is:
explanation: Epsom salt is magnesium sulphate heptahydrate, MgSO₄·7H₂O.

text: The element placed in the second group and third period of the periodic table is:
explanation: Period 3 elements have 3 shells; group 2 elements have 2 valence electrons. Configuration 2,8,2 is magnesium (Z = 12).

text: Which of the following changes CANNOT increase the volume of a fixed mass of gas 4 times?
options: P reduced to one-half and kelvin temperature doubled
P constant, kelvin temperature increased 4 times
T constant, P reduced to one-fourth
explanation: V ∝ T/P. Increasing T four times or reducing P to ¼ makes V four times; halving P and doubling T also gives 2 × 2 = 4 times. Increasing P four times at constant T reduces V to one-fourth.

text: The mass number of an atom whose unipositive ion has 10 electrons and 12 neutrons is:
explanation: A unipositive ion has lost one electron, so the atom has 11 electrons and 11 protons. Mass number = protons + neutrons = 11 + 12 = 23 (sodium).

text: Complete the balanced equation: C₆H₁₂O₆ —(conc. H₂SO₄)→ ______ + 6H₂O
explanation: Conc. sulphuric acid is a dehydrating agent; it removes the elements of water from glucose, leaving a black mass of carbon: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 6C + 6H₂O.

text: The most reactive halogen in the periodic table is:
explanation: Reactivity of halogens decreases down the group. Fluorine, the smallest atom, gains an electron most readily and is the most reactive halogen (and non-metal).

text: The anhydrous salt of potassium which is orange in colour is:
explanation: Potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇, forms orange crystals. Potassium chromate is yellow and potassium permanganate is purple.

text: Which of the following nitrates decomposes on heating to give a metal oxide?
explanation: 2Ca(NO₃)₂ → 2CaO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Potassium and sodium nitrates give nitrites (2KNO₃ → 2KNO₂ + O₂), and ammonium nitrate gives N₂O and water.

text: The element M in the Dobereiner triad Be, M, Ca is:
explanation: Be (9), Mg (24), Ca (40): the atomic mass of Mg is about the mean of Be and Ca, (9 + 40)/2 = 24.5. Mg lies between them in the same group.

text: The relative atomic mass of an element expressed in grams is known as its:
explanation: Relative atomic mass in grams = gram atomic mass (e.g. 12 g for carbon). Gram molecular mass is the relative molecular mass expressed in grams.

text: The element named eka-boron by Mendeleev is now called:
explanation: Mendeleev predicted eka-boron (scandium), eka-aluminium (gallium) and eka-silicon (germanium), which were discovered later.

text: The metalloid of period 3 in the periodic table is:
explanation: Silicon (2,8,4) in period 3 shows properties of both metals and non-metals. Boron is the metalloid of period 2.

text: A chemical reaction in which a compound breaks down on heating into elements or simpler compounds that do NOT recombine on cooling is called:
explanation: In thermal decomposition the change is irreversible (e.g. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂). In thermal dissociation (e.g. NH₄Cl ⇌ NH₃ + HCl) the products recombine on cooling.

text: The acid radical in the formula CaPbO₂ is:
explanation: Calcium is Ca²⁺, so the radical is PbO₂²⁻, the plumbite ion. CaPbO₂ is calcium plumbite.

text: What is observed when excess carbon dioxide is passed through lime water?
options: It first turns milky and then becomes clear again
It turns milky and stays milky
explanation: First insoluble CaCO₃ forms (milkiness): Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O. With excess CO₂ soluble calcium bicarbonate forms and the solution clears: CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂.

text: What is observed when zinc nitrate is heated?
options: A colourless gas is evolved, leaving a black residue
A reddish-brown gas is evolved, leaving a residue that is yellow when hot and white when cold
Violet vapours are given off, leaving no residue
A reddish-brown gas is evolved, leaving a black residue
explanation: 2Zn(NO₃)₂ → 2ZnO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Brown NO₂ is evolved, and the residue ZnO is yellow when hot and white on cooling.

text: Why is it unsafe to store copper sulphate solution in an aluminium vessel?
options: Aluminium is more reactive than copper and displaces it, so the vessel gets corroded
Copper sulphate solution is a strong alkali
Aluminium is less reactive than copper, so copper coats the vessel
Copper sulphate reacts with aluminium oxide to form a poisonous gas
explanation: Aluminium lies above copper in the reactivity series: 2Al + 3CuSO₄ → Al₂(SO₄)₃ + 3Cu. The vessel is eaten away (develops holes) and the solution is spoilt.

text: The relative molecular mass of green vitriol (FeSO₄·7H₂O) is: [Fe = 56, S = 32, H = 1, O = 16]
The formula of the phosphite of a metal X is X₃(PO₃)₂. The formulae of its dichromate and bisulphite are:
explanation: Phosphite PO₃³⁻ has valency 3; three X balance two PO₃³⁻, so X is divalent (X²⁺). With Cr₂O₇²⁻: XCr₂O₇. With HSO₃⁻: X(HSO₃)₂.

text: A crystalline, coloured hydrated salt that evolves sulphur dioxide on strong heating is:
explanation: Green ferrous sulphate crystals lose water and then decompose: 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃. The other salts are white and do not give SO₂.

text: The amount of energy released when an atom in the gaseous state accepts an electron to form an anion is called:
explanation: Electron affinity is the energy released when a neutral gaseous atom gains an electron to form a negative ion. Ionisation energy is the energy needed to remove an electron.

text: Fill in the blank: Zinc is ______ reactive than aluminium.
explanation: In the reactivity series aluminium lies above zinc, so zinc is less reactive than aluminium.

text: An element with two electrons in its outermost shell is likely to be:
options: a noble gas in all cases
explanation: With two valence electrons the atom tends to lose them to attain a stable configuration, forming a positive ion, which is typical of metals (e.g. Mg, Ca). (Helium, with a complete duplet, is the exception.)

text: Hydrogen, although lighter than air, is not collected by the downward displacement of air because:
options: it forms an explosive mixture with air
it is highly soluble in air
it reacts with nitrogen of the air at room temperature
explanation: A mixture of hydrogen and air explodes when it meets a flame. Hydrogen is therefore collected by the downward displacement of water.

text: The percentage of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate (NH₄NO₃) is: [N = 14, H = 1, O = 16]
The balanced form of the equation FeCl₃ + NH₄OH → NH₄Cl + Fe(OH)₃ is:
explanation: Three Cl atoms need 3NH₄Cl, which needs 3NH₄OH; the 3 OH groups form one Fe(OH)₃. Check: Fe 1, Cl 3, N 3, H 12 + 3 = 15 on each side, O 3.

text: A part of the periodic table is given: Period 2: Li Be B C N O F Ne; Period 3: Na Mg Al Si — S Cl Ar. The missing element in period 3 is:
explanation: Between silicon (Z = 14) and sulphur (Z = 16) in period 3 comes phosphorus (Z = 15), which is in group 15 below nitrogen.

text: The type of covalent bond in the chlorine, nitrogen and oxygen molecules respectively is:
explanation: Cl–Cl shares one pair of electrons (single bond), N≡N shares three pairs (triple bond) and O=O shares two pairs (double bond).

text: On dry heating, how can lead carbonate be distinguished from zinc carbonate?
options: Lead carbonate gives brown fumes; zinc carbonate gives none
Lead carbonate leaves a white residue; zinc carbonate leaves a black residue
Lead carbonate leaves a residue that is reddish-brown when hot and yellow when cold; zinc carbonate's residue is yellow when hot and white when cold
explanation: PbCO₃ → PbO + CO₂: PbO is reddish-brown when hot and yellow on cooling. ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂: ZnO is yellow when hot and white on cooling. Both give CO₂.
